summary: notification-service is OOMKilling roughly every 24h due to a memory leak introduced by dep-5402 (v3.8.0, deployed 2026-03-21T00:00Z), which added an unbounded in-memory ConcurrentHashMap TemplateCache. The cache log shows size growing 9000->18000 entries with evictions=0; memory_pct climbs linearly from ~48% to 95-98% then resets on each restart (counter 0->1->2->3 at 03-21T22, 03-22T22, 03-23T20). CPU stays flat at ~25%, ruling out load saturation. The reported Kafka-maintenance/replay theory is contradicted: identical consumer-lag spikes occurred on 03-21 and 03-22 with no maintenance, and memory growth began ~60h before the 03-23T18:00Z retention change. Delayed trade-confirmation emails are a downstream effect of each OOM/GC-thrash episode.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Unbounded in-memory TemplateCache added in dep-5402 leaks memory, causing periodic OOM
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deployment dep-5402 (v3.8.0, 2026-03-21T00:00Z) added a ConcurrentHashMap TemplateCache with no eviction/expiry. Entries accumulate monotonically (~9000/hr, evictions=0), growing the old-gen heap until the container exceeds its limit and is OOMKilled ~every 24h; the restart clears the heap and the cycle repeats. Consumer lag spikes and delayed emails are downstream effects of each OOM/GC-thrashing episode.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5402 adds unbounded ConcurrentHashMap template cache on 03-21T00:00Z
heap saturation -> full-GC thrash WARNs -> OOMKilled exit 137
consumer lag/5xx spikes during each episode -> delayed emails

assumptions: TemplateCache entries are retained per unique template+locale+segment with no bound (log shows evictions=0)
no other memory consumer was introduced in the same window

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka maintenance (retention change) triggered consumer replay that OOMs the consumer
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The reported theory: cfg-2410 (retention 7d->3d) at 03-23T18:00Z caused a replay/lag spike that made the consumer choke and OOM. Only weakly supported: the 03-23 18:00 lag spike coincides with the maintenance, but identical spikes occurred on 03-21 and 03-22 without any maintenance, and the memory sawtooth predates the maintenance by two days.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Memory growth began 2026-03-21T00:00Z, 60+ hours before the 03-23T18:00Z maintenance; the same lag-spike pattern repeats on 03-21/03-22 with no maintenance; and reducing retention removes data rather than forcing a replay. Timing and scope contradict this theory.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External email-provider or infrastructure fault causing backlog/OOM
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A failing external email-provider (no telemetry) or broker fault could stall the consumer and build backlog. Not supported: lag spikes track the OOM/restart cycle, not provider behaviour; kafka logs are clean; no email-provider error evidence exists.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No email-provider errors in logs, kafka logs clean, and lag spikes align with the OOM cycle rather than any external event.

facts.statement: Memory sawtooths from ~48% to 95-98% repeatedly since 03-21T00:00Z, resetting on each restart.
dep-5402 added an in-memory template cache (ConcurrentHashMap) to notification-service at 2026-03-21T00:00Z and is still live, never rolled back.
TemplateCache grows ~9000 entries/hour with evictions=0, indicating no bound/expiry.
Three OOMKilled (exit 137) restarts at 03-21T22:59Z, 03-22T21:59Z, 03-23T19:59Z; restarts counter 0->3.
CPU is flat at ~25% throughout, so the OOM is not driven by CPU/load.
Consumer-lag spikes also occurred on 03-21 and 03-22 without any Kafka maintenance.
The only config change was the kafka retention reduction (7d->3d) at 03-23T18:00Z, ~60h after memory growth began.
5xx error_rate spiked (avg 1.36%, max 13.96%) only during the 03-23T19:00-20:00 OOM episode.
notification-service consumes from shared kafka and calls external email-provider (no telemetry); kafka logs are clean.

assumptions: TemplateCache retains entries keyed by template+locale+userSegment with no eviction or size bound (evictions=0 in logs confirms none occurring).
No other memory consumers were added to notification-service in the same window.
Restart-to-memory-reset mapping is inferred from the sawtooth aligning with each OOM log line.

timeline.event: dep-5402 deploys v3.8.0 adding in-memory TemplateCache; memory_pct begins climbing from ~48%.
Consumer lag spike (avg 810, max 18138) in this bucket.
Third OOMKilled restart; counter 2->3; 5xx error_rate peaks at 13.96%.
Incident INC-004 reported; delayed trade-confirmation emails (~25 min).
Post-restart TemplateCache stats: size=18000 entries, evictions=0 (already regrown).

recommended_actions.action: Roll back notification-service from v3.8.0 (dep-5402) to the prior version to stop the leak immediately.
recommended_actions.rationale: The leak was introduced by dep-5402 and is the verified root cause; rollback restores stable ~48% memory.

recommended_actions.action: If rollback is not possible, bound the TemplateCache (max size / TTL / Caffeine with eviction) and ship as a hotfix.
recommended_actions.rationale: The ConcurrentHashMap has zero evictions and grows unbounded; a bounded cache caps memory.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on memory_pct slope / heap old-gen saturation and a cache-size metric, and raise/verify the container memory limit.
recommended_actions.rationale: The sawtooth was visible for two days before the third restart; slope alerting would catch it earlier.

recommended_actions.action: De-prioritise the Kafka replay theory; verify lag spikes resolve on their own after each restart before considering consumer-side changes.
recommended_actions.rationale: Lag spikes predate and recur independently of the maintenance, so they are an effect, not the cause.

recommended_actions.action: Add memory/eviction regression tests and coverage for new in-memory caches in the notification-service pipeline.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents recurrence of unbounded caches reaching production.

data_gaps: No pod/container memory-limit metric was inspected directly; OOM is inferred from exit code 137 and memory_pct reaching ~98%.
email-provider has no telemetry, so it cannot be fully excluded as a secondary factor, though no evidence implicates it.
Only notification-service and kafka logs were searched; no direct TemplateCache entry-key cardinality data beyond size/evictions counts.
No heap-dump or GC-logs beyond the WARN summaries were available to pinpoint the exact retaining object.

findings.statement: notification-service memory_pct shows a repeated sawtooth: rising linearly from ~48% to 95-98% over ~24h then dropping back to ~48% (restart). Baseline before 03-21T00:00 was flat at ~47-48%.
The memory climb starts exactly at 2026-03-21T00:00Z; the 5-minute-resolution series shows flat ~48% through 03-21T01:00 then steady growth (49.52 -> 72.64 by 11:50).

Deployment dep-5402 shipped to notification-service v3.8.0 at 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z with change 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering' (ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment); status live, never rolled back.
TemplateCache stats logs show unbounded growth with zero evictions: size=9000 entries at 21:00:44 and size=18000 entries at 22:00:34, both with evictions=0 (~9000 entries/hour).
restarts counter (cumulative) went 0 -> 1 at 03-21T22:00 bucket, 1 -> 2 at 03-22T22:00 bucket, 2 -> 3 at 03-23T20:00 bucket.

Three OOMKilled ERROR log lines: 03-21T22:59:50Z, 03-22T21:59:47Z, 03-23T19:59:21Z, each 'container notification-service-7d9f OOMKilled (exit code 137), restarting', each preceded by a burst of 'heap usage ... over 90 (old gen), full GC took' WARNs.
CPU is essentially flat at ~25% (min 21.78, max 28.5) across the whole window, with no rise during memory growth.

consumer_lag spikes (avg 810-2273, max 14375-18137) occur in three buckets: 03-21T22:00 (2273/17161), 03-22T20:00-22:00 (790/17611 and 1589/14375), 03-23T18:00-20:00 (810/18137, 1542/14213). Two of these spikes are NOT after any Kafka maintenance.
The only config change in the window is cfg-2410 on kafka (log.retention.ms 604800000 -> 259200000, i.e. 7d->3d retention) at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z by platform-team.
error_rate (HTTP 5xx) is ~0.2% normally but rises to 1.36%/1.29% avg (max 13.96%) only in the 03-23T19:00 and 20:00 buckets, coinciding with the third OOM, then returns to ~0.2%.

Dependency graph: notification-service consumes from shared kafka and calls external email-provider (no telemetry). Only other deployment in window was auth-service v7.1.4 (jackson bump) on 03-22T13:00.
kafka logs contain only one WARN (deprecated TLS cipher at 03-23T17:17:15Z) and no error/incident-level entries in 17:00-23:59 window.
